result:
Only this one file exists, and the full suite run (46 passing, 1 failing) confirms everything compiles and runs cleanly except for one genuine bug.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` (JUnit 4, self-contained, same-package access to protected members, Java 1.6-compatible syntax). 47 tests total; 46 pass.

**1 failing test exposes a real bug:**

- `testConstructorThrowsNpeForNullTimeZone` — `FastDatePrinter`'s class javadoc explicitly documents: `@throws NullPointerException if pattern, timeZone, or locale is null`. The constructor only assigns `mTimeZone = timeZone` without a null check, and `init()`/`parsePattern()` only dereferences `mTimeZone` when the pattern contains a `z` or `Z` token. So constructing `new FastDatePrinter("yyyy-MM-dd", null, Locale.US)` succeeds silently instead of throwing, violating the documented contract (the `null` would only surface later, and non-deterministically, as an NPE inside `format()` via `new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)` — but only for patterns that end up constructing a `GregorianCalendar`, and never at all for callers who only use `format(Calendar, ...)` overloads).

All other tests pass, covering: numeric/text field formatting (year, month, day, hour variants h/H/k/K, am/pm, weekday text, era), zero-padding/multi-digit edge cases, `Z`/`ZZ` timezone offsets (positive and negative), literal/quoted text and escaped quotes, invalid pattern letters, all `format(Object/Date/Calendar/long, ...)` overloads including unsupported-type and `null` error cases, accessors, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, serialization round-trip, and the protected `parsePattern`/`parseToken`/`selectNumberRule` helpers.
